question.worked_solution:
The variable $y$ is being *multiplied* by $-2.$ To isolate $y,$ we perform the *opposite* operation, which is *dividing* by $-2.$ Remember to perform the same operation on both sides.

Also, when multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2y\,\, & >\,\,18 \\ \frac{-2y}{-2}\,\, & <\,\,\frac{18}{-2} \\ \frac{-2y}{-2}\,\, & <\,\,-9\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can cancel a common factor of $-2$ from both the numerator and denominator.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-2y}{-2} & <-9 \\ \frac{\cancel{-2}y}{\cancel{-2}} & <-9 \\ y & <-9\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $y<-9.$
